messages:
maria: Heads-up — new model intake: Aurora-13B gguf (community release). Need a quantization plan + quick calibration run. Priority: keep chat-quality within 5% of fp16 but reduce token cost. Can we sketch a fast path (smoke -> full calib -> deploy)?

jonathan: What baseline metrics do we have for fp16? please paste top-level eval (chat winrate / avg ROUGE / latency)

maria: FP16 baseline (local eval): chat winrate 0.78, avg BLEU-like sim 0.62, median token-latency 45ms on A100-80GB. nb: these are single-turn sims.

quant-bot: Auto-report: model size 13.1B, fp16 footprint ~24GB, kv-cache delta ~8GB. Recommended quant candidates: int8 PTQ, fp8 hybrid A, gguf-quant for distro. Quick sim-est cost reduction estimate: int8 ~2.8x, fp8 ~1.9x, gguf (hybrid) ~2.4x. :rocket:

liam: Target infra? hosted or dedicated? Important for kernel choices (triton autotune vs custom kernels)

maria: Hosted first (customers will use hosted API). If we need a dedicated run for regression isolation we can spin one up.

jonathan: Proposed minimal plan:
- smoke: int8 PTQ (per-channel) + quick eval on chat_eval_v2 (1k prompts)
- if int8 >5% regression -> try fp8 dynamic/e4f and gguf hybrid (kv-cache fp16)
- calibration: run 2k calibration samples (diverse convs) and collect logits/rank-deltas
- final: run full 10k eval and head-to-head with fp16

maria: Agree. Add notes: prefer symmetric quant for int8 to avoid bias, but test asym for tail-layers. Also we should capture hallucination rate on a small factual suite.

liam: Quick conversion snippets for the smoke run (putting here so infra can reproduce):
```bash
# convert to gguf int8 per-channel (sample CLI)
quant-cli convert --input aurora-13b.gguf --out aurora-13b-int8.gguf --mode int8_perchannel --calib-file calib-2k.json

# fp8 candidate
quant-cli convert --input aurora-13b.gguf --out aurora-13b-fp8.gguf --mode fp8_dynamic --mantissa 6
```

jonathan: Calibration dataset question — use chat_eval_v2 seeded + a small set of recent customer prompts? We want distribution match.

maria: yes use chat_eval_v2 (1.5k) + 500 recent-prod-samples (anonymized). I'll drop the list in the drive doc: https://docs.google.com/drive/aurora-calib (please ping if access issues). :eyes:

quant-bot: Calibration quick-check complete (smoke): int8 PTQ median delta vs fp16: 0.042 sim-score drop, fp8 dynamic: 0.018, gguf-hybrid: 0.026. Latency gains: int8 2.9x, fp8 1.8x, gguf 2.3x.

sophia: Product constraint reminder — we must cap visible quality regressions to <5% rate on core chat flows, else block rollout. Also need rollback plan.

maria: OK plan:
1) Smoke (today): run int8 PTQ per-channel on 2k calib, quick eval (1k prompts). If sim-drop <=3% -> proceed to canary.
2) If int8 fails (>3% and <7%) -> try fp8 dynamic and gguf-hybrid runs; pick variant with best tradeoff.
3) Canary (48h): route 5% traffic on hosted, monitor winrate/latency/errors. Auto-fallback to fp16 if winrate drops >5% or errors spike.
4) Post-mortem + rollout doc.

liam: I'll schedule a smoke-capable job on hosted infra and add the kernel flags: --prefer-int8-kernels --batch-threshold 8. Starting in ~30m.

jonathan: I'll prepare the meas script (rank-deltas, nll comparison, hallucination checklist). Dropping eval script in github: https://git.redwood.ai/aurora/quant-eval

maria: Perfect. Tagging the small follow-ups: @jonathan please pick the calibration subset; @liam please collect perf traces; @sophia will sign off on canary criteria. :+1:

sophia: Got it. Will validate canary metrics and get legal/security signoff if prod samples included.

quant-bot: Reminder: add tags to the model entry: [aurora-13b, gguf, quant-candidate, intake-2026-03]

maria: thanks all — will post the quick smoke results in this thread once done.
